item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01495","case1_error":"Misdivides Grenada’s supplies between bases, omits guns, imposes equal totals, and makes additional numerical errors.","case2_error":"Identifies the first annual increase as the current year and reports 300 despite calculating the third-year value, 675.","reason":"Case 1 constructs invalid supply relations and miscalculates; case 2 selects the wrong year’s quantity.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01496","case1_error":"Answer marker says 300, but the explanation correctly calculates remaining savings as $200.","case2_error":"Calculates jewelry spending without subtracting the $40 already spent on the sweater.","reason":"Case 1 has only an answer-marker conflict; case 2 omits an expenditure from its balance equation.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J01497","case1_error":"Doubles the second country’s stay for the third, although both other stays should double the first country’s stay.","case2_error":"Invents a base and two side areas; the question’s height and width do not unambiguously specify the uncovered shoebox area.","reason":"Case 1 uses the wrong comparison baseline. Case 2 involves materially ambiguous geometry: a planar reading gives 8, while literal shoebox coverage lacks dimensions.","judgment":"uncertain"},{"pair_id":"J01498","case1_error":"Multiplies miles directly by dollars per gallon, omitting conversion from miles to gallons using fuel efficiency.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates the correctly written sum 132 + 35 as 144 instead of 167.","reason":"Case 1 uses an erroneous cost relation; case 2 makes a numerical evaluation error in a correct expression.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01499","case1_error":"Omits Ted’s four eaten cookies when calculating the final remainder.","case2_error":"Equates chicken guests with all 80 guests instead of using x + 3x = 80.","reason":"Case 1 omits a required subtraction; case 2 confuses a subgroup count with the total when applying the ratio.","judgment":"different"}]}
